result.summary: The surface of go.yaml.in/yaml/v4 v4.0.0-rc.2 consists of resolve.go and yaml.go. They implement YAML scalar resolution, the public Marshal/Unmarshal API, struct field reflection and event formatting. I checked the init functions, the imports and the encoded data: there is no network, exec, filesystem, environment or unsafe use, no files missing from the source repository, and nothing beyond what a YAML library needs.

findings.title: Init functions only populate static tables
findings.detail: resolve.go has two init functions that fill in in-memory lookup tables: resolveTable, resolveMap and the long/short tag maps. yaml.go has one init that caches the reflect.Type of the Unmarshaler interface. None of them does I/O, touches the environment, uses the network or patches other code.

findings.title: Base64 use is standard !!binary encoding
findings.detail: Base64 appears only in encodeBase64, which encodes non-UTF-8 strings as !!binary scalars during marshalling. This is standard YAML behaviour and the file contains no embedded payload.
